script:
This is the New Saint Croix Union for Monday, September 28. Here is the week's news.

Washington County commissioners last Tuesday were asked to certify a proposed property-tax levy of one hundred sixty-one million, nine hundred eighty-six thousand, five hundred dollars, for taxes payable in 2027. The net levy moves from one hundred forty-eight point nine million dollars in 2026 to one hundred sixty point seven million in 2027, a seven point nine percent change. The net tax rate moves from twenty-four point forty-five percent to twenty-five point fifty-two. On a residential homestead valued at four hundred thirty thousand, six hundred dollars, the general levy, the Land and Water Legacy line, and the railroad levy come to one thousand thirty-three dollars this year and one thousand ninety-three dollars for 2027, a difference of sixty dollars. That example assumes the home's value rose one point three percent. The Land and Water Legacy amount moves from one point two million to one point three million. The railroad levy stays six hundred sixty thousand dollars. A Community Development Agency levy would be capped at seven million, two hundred eighty-three thousand, four hundred forty-six dollars. The same morning included a Valley Paving contract of three hundred fifty-nine thousand, seven hundred ninety-six dollars and seventy-five cents for a traffic signal at Valley Creek Road and Eagle Creek Lane in Woodbury. The engineer's estimate was five hundred fifty-six thousand, six hundred thirteen dollars and twenty cents. Certification is due September 30. A public budget hearing is listed for December 1, after six in the evening. Final adoption is listed for December 15. The meeting was at nine in the morning in the County Board Room.

The Stillwater-area school board last Tuesday was asked to adopt a preliminary property-tax levy for 2027. No dollar amount is printed. Levy revenue is about twenty-nine percent of the district's general fund budget. State law requires a proposed levy by September 30. The board can adopt the September estimates, or it can certify the word Maximum. A dollar amount adopted in September cannot be raised later. The presentation recommends certifying Maximum, so later state adjustments can still be included. After October 1 the levy can only move down. Final adoption is December 22. The same meeting would set a truth-in-taxation hearing for December 8 at six in the evening at Oak Park Learning Center, sixty-three fifty-five Osman Avenue North. Consent includes a Stillwater Area High School band and orchestra trip to New Orleans on March 23 through 27, 2026. The agenda includes a closed session to consider an offer to buy or sell real property. The board met at five-thirty in the evening at that building.

Oakdale's city council last Tuesday was asked to consider a three-story self-storage building at sixty-eight fifteen Fifty-fifth Street North, and two million, eight hundred eighty-four thousand, eight hundred thirty-two dollars and sixty-two cents in claims for September 9 through September 22. P 4 Properties wants a building with a twenty-six thousand square-foot footprint and a rental office. The lot is vacant, about eight point two acres, with about three acres of wetlands on the east half. It is zoned general industrial, and self-storage is not allowed there. The request would rezone it to light industrial, shift the comprehensive-plan guidance to industrial-office, grant a setback variance, and approve a preliminary plat. The code requires three hundred fifty feet from the nearest residential property. The nearest one is about two hundred fifty-three feet away. The council would also let the city administrator and the finance director sell up to twenty million dollars in bonds for improvements, the local sales tax, and capital projects. The sale is proposed for October 15, if the interest rate stays at or below five point five percent. The bonds would mature no later than February 1, 2053. Planet Fitness has offered twenty-one pieces of used fitness equipment, about one hundred fifty-seven thousand, four hundred thirty-eight dollars, for the fitness room in the new city hall and police department. Accepting the gift takes a two-thirds vote. The meeting was at seven in the evening at the Discovery Center, forty-four forty-four Hadley Avenue North.

Stillwater's planning commission last Wednesday heard a gym at two-twenty Commercial Street and a food truck at two-twenty-five Main Street North. The gym would be a private membership studio for strength training in an existing building of about twenty-six hundred square feet. The applicant expects fifteen to twenty people at a time, from five in the morning to ten at night, seven days a week. The lot has four off-street spaces. The city's parking table for a health club would call for twenty-six. Staff recommended approval of the conditional-use permit. River Siren Brewing applied to park the Chuletacos food truck in the lot at two-twenty-five Main Street North from three in the afternoon to ten at night, up to seven days a week, and leave overnight. City code allows one seasonal food truck on a property at a time. An interim-use permit is required because this truck would stay more than four days a week. The permit would last up to a year. Staff recommended approval. The meeting was at seven in the evening at two-sixteen Fourth Street North.

Woodbury's city council last Wednesday was asked to set a preliminary 2027 property-tax levy of sixty million, eight hundred fifty-five thousand, five hundred ninety-two dollars, including a two-hundred-fifty-thousand-dollar Housing and Redevelopment Authority levy. The city levy in the resolution text is sixty million, six hundred five thousand, five hundred ninety-two dollars. The total is five hundred ninety-three thousand thirty dollars below the budget-workshop figure. Staff says that change would move the estimated increase on a median-value home from eighty-one dollars to sixty-five. The estimated city tax rate would be thirty-four point two eight one percent, a three point seven percent change. The preliminary 2027 budget is one hundred sixty-six million, two hundred forty-two thousand twenty-five dollars. A Truth-in-Taxation meeting is listed for Wednesday, December 9, at seven-thirty in the evening. The same night included a proposed pause, for as long as one year, on new data centers and on expansions of the existing sites at five hundred, five-fifteen, and four-oh-one Bielenberg Drive. Staff says there are no current or pending applications for new data centers, and lists no budget impact. Pulte Homes of Minnesota asks to rezone fifty-three acres north of Dale Road and west of Cottage Grove Drive for a subdivision called Nottingham. The land is zoned urban reserve and guided low density. The first phase is twenty-eight acres and thirty-five single-family lots. The Planning Commission recommended approval six to zero on September 14. The council met at seven-forty in the evening at City Hall, or right after a Housing and Redevelopment Authority meeting.

A Woodbury workshop the same afternoon covered a mass-casualty exercise and the public-safety campus. An attached letter puts the campus project budget at about fifty-nine point three million dollars, funded mainly by a voter-approved fifty-million-dollar local option sales tax. The workshop was at five-thirty in the Ash Conference Rooms at City Hall. The agenda says it was not a public hearing and would not take formal votes.

The Highway 243 bridge between Franconia Township and Osceola closes mid-October 2026 through fall 2027 while Minnesota and Wisconsin replace the 1953 span. The new bridge is a concrete beam structure with three piers on the same alignment, plus a shared-use path on the north side of Highway 243 from Osceola Landing, across the river, to the Village of Osceola. The north detour is the Highway 8 crossing at Taylors Falls. The south detour is the Highway 36 Stillwater crossing. Osceola Landing's north boat launch and parking lot have been closed since eight in the morning on Monday, September 14, through late summer 2028. Construction is anticipated to finish in fall 2028.

The North St. Paul–Maplewood–Oakdale school board meets tonight at six to certify a proposed 2026 payable 2027 property-tax levy of sixty-nine million, one hundred seventeen thousand, sixty-four dollars. That total is eight hundred seventy-six thousand, seven hundred thirty-eight dollars below the payable-2026 figure of sixty-nine million, nine hundred ninety-three thousand, eight hundred two dollars, a one point three percent change. The director of finance recommends certifying the proposed levy at the maximum, because final levy authority may still change. The board adopts the final levy in December. Certification is due to the county auditors by September 30. The general-fund levy would fall to thirty-five million, seven hundred seventy-five thousand, nine hundred eighty-two dollars, down two million, one hundred sixty-five thousand, nine hundred sixty-five dollars, or five point seven percent. The community-service levy would rise to one million, seven hundred forty-five thousand, four hundred fifty-two dollars, up twenty point nine percent. Debt service would rise to thirty-one million, five hundred ninety-five thousand, six hundred thirty dollars, up ten point nine percent. The OPEB debt-service levy would drop from two million, one hundred thirty thousand, six hundred ninety-one dollars to zero. Consent includes three grants: five thousand dollars from the Minnesota State Arts Board for the Tartan High School concert choir, five hundred dollars from the NEA, and seventy-five thousand dollars from the Minneapolis Foundation. The grant sheet quotes state law that acceptance may not be for religious or sectarian purposes. The board is also asked to revise policies that include literacy and the READ Act, graduation requirements, enrollment of nonresident students, and internet, technology, and cell-phone use, and to adopt a new policy on responsible use of artificial intelligence throughout the district. Speakers sign in and have two to four minutes. The comment period lasts no longer than thirty minutes.

Lake Elmo's planning commission meets tonight at six-thirty at thirty-eight eighty Laverne Avenue North. Lisa Smith asks to expand the city's MUSA boundary, served by Oakdale, and re-guide forty-four fifty-five Olson Lake Trail North to RSFS. The agenda says the reason is a noncompliant septic system. Doug Biever asks for flexibility from the twenty-five percent impervious-surface cap at eleven thousand fifty-five Thirty-second Street North to build a new garage and move the driveway. The commission is also asked to report that a sale of city property in the old village, including the old fire hall and parks buildings, would comply with the comprehensive plan. The agenda does not print a sale price or a buyer. The October 14 meeting is canceled. The next listed meeting is October 26.

Stillwater's Parks and Recreation Commission meets tonight at seven on a Lumberjack Landing guiding document and a playground replacement at Prairie Park. The generated agenda does not print a meeting place, a dollar figure, or a recommended action on either item. Open-forum remarks are limited to five minutes.

Washington County's library board meets tonight from six-thirty to eight at R.H. Stafford Library in Woodbury to hear a 2027 budget presentation that lists a county net levy of ten million, nine hundred eighteen thousand, eight hundred dollars. That levy line moves from ten million, three hundred thirty-six thousand, two hundred dollars in 2026, a five point sixty-four percent change. Non-levy revenue is listed at six hundred thirty-four thousand, nine hundred dollars. Personnel would be seven million, seven hundred eighty-five thousand, nine hundred dollars, services and charges one million, nine hundred ninety-three thousand, three hundred, and materials and supplies one million, seven hundred seventy-four thousand, five hundred. The same meeting includes a Strategic Facilities Plan workshop with MSR Design and a construction update on Park Grove and R.H. Stafford. July 27 minutes in the packet say Park Grove demolition is complete, the entry foundation is in, and water damage led to replacing all exterior walls while keeping structural steel and the roof. The meeting is in Savannah A, lower level, inside Central Parks.

Times and documents are in the show notes.
